residential_rent_dispute.explanation: Ordinary landlord–tenant rent disputes generally fall outside RERA. Use your state’s rent authority or civil remedies instead.

deposit_refund.explanation: Security-deposit refund disputes between landlord and tenant are typically handled under rent/tenancy law, not RERA, unless the dispute is against a RERA-registered promoter/project.

eviction_threat.explanation: Eviction and recovery of possession for residential tenancies are governed by state rent/tenancy acts and courts — not RERA grievance for ordinary landlord–tenant cases.

essential_services.explanation: Withholding essential services in a residential tenancy is usually a rent-authority / civil matter under state tenancy law, not a RERA complaint against a promoter.

promoter_allottee.explanation: Disputes between an allottee and a RERA-registered promoter (or real estate agent) may be filed as a complaint under Section 31 of the RERA Act, 2016.

builder_delay.explanation: Delay in possession or related promoter obligations for a registered real estate project may give rise to a RERA complaint; check your state RERA portal for procedure.
